xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3148: Pushed rework commit does not trigger re-review: review stays blocked at a stale SHA while feedback is redelivered, burning agent context

plan.title: Pushed rework commit does not trigger re-review: review stays blocked at a stale SHA while feedback is redelivered, burning agent context
plan.author: agent:k3[1m]

narratives.Problem: On PAN-3093 (2026-07-26) a review convoy blocked at HEAD cd81b757; the work agent fixed the findings, committed, and pushed (a0bd351134), but nothing detected the new HEAD. review_status stayed blocked against the stale SHA, the identical BLOCKED feedback was re-delivered to the agent 3x (context burned to 81%, $60->$85), and the agent idled 'waiting for a new run ID' that could only be minted by the re-review nobody dispatched. `pan review restart` fixed it in one command. Verified root causes: (1) checkPostReviewCommits (src/lib/cloister/deacon.ts:1580) skips non-passed issues, so blocked+drift is never examined; (2) reviewedAtCommit is only snapshotted on passed verdicts (legacy-routes.ts:316, done.ts:159), so blocked verdicts have no anchor to compare; (3) deliverReviewVerdictFeedbackPromise (review-verdict-feedback.ts:146) calls messageAgent without a dedupKey, bypassing the existing exactly-once delivery infrastructure.
narratives.Proposal: Four changes, one per issue ask: (1) snapshot reviewedAtCommit on blocked verdicts at all three verdict sites, as a second write AFTER the durable verdict + feedback kickoff (preserves PAN-2524); (2) extend checkPostReviewCommits to blocked reviews — on real anchor drift (with a reviewerVerdicts-derived anchor fallback for legacy rows and a two-patrol-tick HEAD-stability debounce), reset review to pending and re-dispatch the convoy, mirroring the proven passed path; (3) pass a dedupKey (review-feedback:<issue>:<sha256(verdict|runId|anchor)[:16]>) through messageAgent's existing keyed-delivery infrastructure, with unkeyed fallback for ACP/Channels targets that cannot enforce keys; (4) thread DeliveryResult.deduplicated into MessageDeliveryOutcome and, on the 2nd suppressed re-delivery for one key, surface one needs-you escalation via surfaceIssueFeedbackNeedsYou. Plus a work-prompt line telling agents that pushed rework while blocked auto-triggers re-review (never wait for a run ID).
narratives.NonGoals:
- Extending drift detection to reviewStatus:'failed' (PAN-794 infra-recovery design space)
- Persisting feedback-delivery attempt counts to the journal or SQLite (in-memory map is sufficient, D4)
- Deduplicating the append-only feedback file / feedback[] history (message-level only, D3)
- Changing `pan review restart`, review convoy prompts, or reviewer sub-role fan-out
- Any dashboard frontend change
- Fixing PAN-3147 (orchestrator liveness-vs-verdict read) — separately filed

autoDecisions.summary: D1: Patrol mirrors the passed-path reset + spawnReviewRoleForIssue({force:true}) instead of reusing the `pan review restart` HTTP route
autoDecisions.rationale: Same proven code path as the passed-case drift handling; no deacon self-call over HTTP.

autoDecisions.summary: D2: Two-patrol-tick HEAD-stability debounce before auto-dispatching re-review for a blocked issue
autoDecisions.rationale: Auto-dispatching on first observed drift could fire while the agent is still mid-rework (agents push per item); requiring ~1-2 min of HEAD stability rescues a finished-and-waiting agent within ~2 minutes while a still-pushing agent keeps resetting the clock.

autoDecisions.summary: D3: Dedup at the agent-message level via existing dedupKey infrastructure, not the append-only feedback file
autoDecisions.rationale: The context damage is the repeated message; tmux markers, the supervisor key store, and keyed mail filenames already provide the needed durability with zero schema changes.

autoDecisions.summary: D4: Escalation counter is an in-memory module-level map, not a persisted ReviewStatus field
autoDecisions.rationale: The observed redelivery loop ran within one host lifetime; persisting would require a ReviewStatus field + SQLite column, disproportionate for a defence-in-depth signal.

autoDecisions.summary: D5: Scope is blocked verdicts only; reviewStatus:'failed' untouched
autoDecisions.rationale: 'failed' is the infra-failure path with its own PAN-794 recovery design; mixing it in would be unreviewed scope creep.

autoDecisions.summary: D6: Ask #2 handled by the primary fix + work-prompt guidance, not a new status surface
autoDecisions.rationale: Verified the 'waiting for a new run ID' sentence appears nowhere in src/ — it is agent-derived reasoning, so the durable fix is removing the condition and instructing the agent not to wait.

items.title: Snapshot reviewedAtCommit on blocked review verdicts at all three verdict sites

expected_outputs: both named test files pass including the new blocked-verdict anchor cases

narrative.Action: PRD WI-1. At each of the three blocked-verdict write sites, snapshot the workspace HEAD via snapshotWorkspaceHeadsPromise and record it as reviewedAtCommit in a SECOND setReviewStatusSync call placed AFTER the durable verdict write and feedback-delivery kickoff (PAN-2524 ordering — never fold the anchor into the pre-delivery update). (1) src/cli/commands/specialists/done.ts: after the feedback-delivery block (~line 243), if options.status === 'blocked', best-effort snapshot + setReviewStatusSync(normalizedIssueId, { reviewedAtCommit }); extend the line-126 comment to document the blocked second-write. (2) src/dashboard/server/routes/specialists/legacy-routes.ts: add a sibling to the `specialist === 'review' && status === 'passed'` guard (~line 316) for status === 'blocked', placed after the feedback-delivery block (~line 493), same snapshot body. (3) src/lib/cloister/deacon-review-signals.ts: the fallback synthesis already computes fallbackHead (~line 240); add `...(fallbackHead ? { reviewedAtCommit: fallbackHead } : {})` to the setReviewStatusSync call when synthesis.verdict === 'blocked'. Extend the two named test files with blocked-verdict cases asserting the anchor lands and the write happens after the feedback write (call order).

items.title: Given a blocked verdict via `pan specialists done`, when the command completes, then getReviewStatusSync(issueId).reviewedAtCommit returns the workspace HEAD anchor and the feedback file write precedes the anchor write in call order
Given a blocked verdict via POST /api/specialists/done, when the route completes, then reviewedAtCommit is persisted with the workspace HEAD anchor
Given the deacon fallback synthesis produces a blocked verdict with a computed fallbackHead, when setReviewStatusSync runs, then the update includes reviewedAtCommit: fallbackHead

Given the snapshot probe throws or returns undefined at any site, when the verdict path completes, then the blocked verdict and feedback delivery still succeed with reviewedAtCommit absent (best-effort, no new failure mode)
Extend checkPostReviewCommits to detect HEAD drift on blocked reviews and re-dispatch

expected_outputs: existing deacon-ci-retry and post-review-rebase tests stay green

narrative.Action: PRD WI-2, decisions D1/D2, hazards H3-H6. In checkPostReviewCommits (src/lib/cloister/deacon.ts:1569): (a) change the gate at line 1580 to also admit status.reviewStatus === 'blocked' (passed/readyForMerge behavior unchanged). (b) Anchor resolution for blocked rows: status.reviewedAtCommit, else if every Object.values(status.reviewerVerdicts ?? {}) has an identical non-empty atCommit use that, else skip with a rate-limited log ('blocked without anchor — cannot detect drift', at most once per issue per patrol-hour). (c) Debounce (blocked only): module-level Map<issueId, anchor>; first drifted observation records the current anchor and skips; second consecutive patrol tick with the SAME current anchor proceeds; any status or anchor change deletes the entry. (d) On confirmed blocked drift: setReviewStatusSync(issueId, { reviewStatus: 'pending', readyForMerge: false, reviewedAtCommit: undefined, reviewRetryCount: 0, recoveryStartedAt: undefined }) — do NOT touch testStatus/testNotes/reviewNotes (H5) — then re-dispatch through the same advancing-slot gate + spawnReviewRoleForIssue({ force: true }) block the passed path uses (deacon.ts:1642-1672), action string: 'Re-dispatched review for <issue>: rework commit after BLOCKED verdict (<old> → <new>)'. (e) Benign drift on a blocked row advances reviewedAtCommit exactly like the passed path. Reuse evaluateWorkspaceAnchorDrift unchanged (polyrepo-safe, NFR-3). Create tests/unit/lib/cloister/deacon-post-blocked-review-commits.test.ts mirroring tests/lib/cloister/deacon-ci-retry.test.ts structure: drifted blocked → first tick records only, second tick resets + dispatches; benign → anchor advances, no reset; derived anchor from agreeing reviewerVerdicts works; disagreeing verdicts → skip; debounce entry cleared on status change mid-window.

items.title: Given reviewStatus 'blocked' with an anchor, when the workspace HEAD advances with a real tree change and holds for two patrol ticks, then the patrol resets reviewStatus to 'pending' and spawns a review convoy at the new HEAD
Given the same blocked setup with drift observed on only the first patrol tick, when the second tick has not run, then no reset and no dispatch occurs (debounce)
Given a blocked row with a same-tree (benign) HEAD move, when the patrol runs, then reviewedAtCommit advances to the new anchor and reviewStatus stays 'blocked' with no dispatch

Given a blocked row with no reviewedAtCommit but uniform reviewerVerdicts[*].atCommit, when the patrol evaluates drift, then it uses the derived anchor; given disagreeing atCommit values, then it skips the issue
Given the blocked-drift reset fires, when setReviewStatusSync is called, then the update preserves testStatus, testNotes, and reviewNotes and resets reviewRetryCount and recoveryStartedAt
Deliver review-verdict feedback with a dedupKey through the existing keyed-delivery infrastructure

expected_outputs: review-verdict-feedback tests pass including keyed + ACP-fallback cases

narrative.Action: PRD WI-3, decision D3, hazard H2. In src/lib/cloister/review-verdict-feedback.ts: add `runId?: string` to DeliverReviewVerdictFeedbackOptions; compute dedupKey = 'review-feedback:' + issueId.toLowerCase() + ':' + createHash('sha256').update([opts.verdict, opts.runId ?? '', existingStatus?.reviewedAtCommit ?? ''].join('|')).digest('hex').slice(0,16) (satisfies DEDUP_KEY_RE in src/lib/tmux-dedup.ts:45); pass { owesRework: true, dedupKey } to messageAgent (line 146). Wrap the messageAgent call: on the 'cannot enforce a dedup key' error thrown for ACP/Channels targets (src/lib/agents/delivery.ts:485-492), retry once unkeyed ({ owesRework: true }) and log the fallback — delivery beats dedup. In src/lib/cloister/deacon-review-signals.ts:252 pass runId: state.reviewRunId in the delivery opts. Extend tests/unit/lib/cloister/review-verdict-feedback.test.ts: messageAgent receives the dedupKey; same verdict+anchor produces the same key across calls, different anchors produce different keys; keyed-throw falls back to unkeyed and still delivers.

items.title: Given two delivery calls for the same issue, verdict, and anchor, when messageAgent is invoked, then both calls carry the identical dedupKey matching /^[A-Za-z0-9:_-]+$/
Given delivery calls for the same verdict at different anchors (or different runIds), when keys are computed, then the dedupKeys differ

Given messageAgent throws 'cannot enforce a dedup key' (ACP/Channels target), when deliverReviewVerdictFeedbackPromise runs, then it retries unkeyed and the feedback reaches the agent (agentMessageSent true)
Given the deacon fallback synthesis delivers blocked feedback, when it calls deliverReviewVerdictFeedback, then opts include runId: state.reviewRunId
Escalate to needs-you on the 2nd suppressed (deduplicated) re-delivery for one key

expected_outputs: escalation tests pass: first suppression silent, second escalates once, third does not re-escalate

narrative.Action: PRD WI-4, decision D4. In src/lib/agents/messaging.ts: thread the existing DeliveryResult.deduplicated flag into MessageDeliveryOutcome on the live-delivery return paths (the plain keyed path ~line 167 and resumeThenDeliverKeyed ~line 150) as `deduplicated?: boolean`. In src/lib/cloister/review-verdict-feedback.ts: add a module-level Map<string, number> keyed by dedupKey; when the delivery result has deduplicated === true, increment the counter, and at count === 2 call surfaceIssueFeedbackNeedsYou(issueId, 'Review feedback for this verdict was already delivered to the agent; the pipeline re-triggered delivery 3+ times — possible stuck loop. Investigate before the agent context burns.', { specialist: 'review-agent', feedbackPath: fileResult.filePath }) exactly once per key; reset the counter when a delivery for the same key completes non-deduplicated. Tests in tests/unit/lib/cloister/review-verdict-feedback.test.ts: first deduplicated result does not escalate; second escalates once; third does not re-escalate; a fresh (non-deduplicated) delivery resets the count.

items.title: Given a delivery result with deduplicated true, when it is the first suppression for its key, then no needs-you escalation is surfaced
Given a second consecutive deduplicated result for the same key, when the counter reaches 2, then surfaceIssueFeedbackNeedsYou fires exactly once naming the issue and the repeated-delivery loop
Given a third deduplicated result for the same key, when the counter increments again, then no additional escalation fires
Given a messageAgent return type, when reading MessageDeliveryOutcome, then it exposes deduplicated?: boolean threaded from DeliveryResult
Work prompt: pushed rework while BLOCKED auto-triggers re-review — never wait for a run ID

expected_outputs: grep shows the new blocked-rework bullet next to the existing passed-review bullet (~line 374)

narrative.Action: PRD WI-5, decision D6 (ask #2 — the 'waiting for a new run ID' standoff is agent-derived reasoning, so instruct the agent directly). In src/lib/cloister/prompts/work.md next to the existing 'If you make commits AFTER review already passed' bullet (~line 374), add in the same style: '**If you push commits while review is BLOCKED:** the pipeline detects the new HEAD within a couple of patrol cycles and re-dispatches review automatically. Never wait for a "new run ID" — if your rework is complete and pushed and no review starts, invoke `/rebase-and-submit` (`pan review request {{ISSUE_ID}} -m "Addressed feedback: <summary>"`).'
